title: Best VPN & Proxy Tools Compared
metaDescription: NordVPN, ExpressVPN, Surfshark and ProxyMesh compared on logging, streaming, device limits, security features and support, scored on one published rubric.
intro: A VPN or proxy decides how much of your online activity others can see, and many services make promises that are hard to check. This page compares three VPNs and a proxy service on the same criteria, and each rating is worked out from the table.

verdict.summary: On these five criteria ExpressVPN and NordVPN tie for the top score; ExpressVPN is listed first only because ties are ordered alphabetically. Both have audited no-logs policies, work with major streaming services and have strong security features; NordVPN covers 10 devices, and ExpressVPN 10 to 14 depending on the plan. Surfshark VPN scores a little lower but allows unlimited devices, which makes it good value for families. ProxyMesh scores lowest: it is a rotating-IP proxy for web scraping and automation, logs all usage and adds no encryption, so it isn't a substitute for a VPN. Speed isn't one of the criteria: it depends on your connection, the server and the protocol, and we haven't measured it.

bestFor.reason: Audited no-logs policy, RAM-only servers and reliable streaming support
Advanced security options and multiple independent audits of its no-logs policy
Unlimited device connections and an audited no-logs policy
Rotating IP addresses designed for automated tasks

pro_tips: Always test a VPN's speed during your typical usage hours before committing to a long-term plan.
A VPN hides your IP address from websites, but cookies and sign-ins can still identify you, so pair it with a browser that blocks trackers.
Avoid free VPNs for sensitive activities - they often log data or inject ads to make money.
Enable your VPN's kill switch feature to prevent data leaks if the connection drops unexpectedly.
Choose servers closer to your location for better speeds, but farther servers for better geo-unblocking.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a VPN and a proxy?
faqs.answer: VPNs encrypt all your internet traffic and route it through the VPN's servers, while proxies usually handle only the apps you point at them and add no encryption of their own. VPNs provide better privacy and security for general use.

faqs.question: Are free VPNs safe to use?
faqs.answer: Many are not. Free VPNs have to make money somehow, and some have been caught logging and selling browsing data, injecting ads or shipping malware. A reputable paid VPN with an independently audited no-logs policy is safer; if you need a free option, use the free tier of a provider that sells paid plans and publishes audits of its no-logs policy.

faqs.question: Will a VPN slow down my internet connection?
faqs.answer: Usually a little, because your traffic is encrypted and goes through the VPN server. How much depends on your connection, how far away and how busy the server is, and the protocol: modern protocols such as WireGuard (which NordVPN's NordLynx is built on) and ExpressVPN's Lightway are designed to keep the overhead low. Speed isn't scored on this page, because we haven't measured it.

faqs.question: Can I use a VPN to access Netflix from other countries?
faqs.answer: Many VPNs can access geo-blocked content, but streaming services actively block VPN traffic. ExpressVPN and NordVPN are most reliable for streaming, though this violates most streaming services' terms of use.

faqs.question: How do I know if my VPN actually protects my privacy?
faqs.answer: Look for independently audited no-logs policies, open-source apps, and transparency reports. Avoid services that haven't been audited or have unclear privacy policies.
